editorial:
Imagine you are sitting in a quiet train station early in the morning, just waiting for your mom to arrive. You are pregnant and thinking about your future, but then someone you haven't seen in a decade walks through the door. That is exactly where you find Alice. The vibe here is very intimate and tense because the whole story happens in one spot. You get to watch this awkward, emotional reunion unfold in real time, and you can really feel the stress and sadness between the father and daughter as they try to figure out where they stand after ten years of silence.

What really makes this work is the acting. The two leads do a great job of showing emotion without needing a ton of dialogue. It is a slow burn, so if you like big explosions or fast plots, this might feel a bit sluggish. However, if you love deep character studies, you will enjoy it.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a heavy emotional release. After spending the time arguing and remembering the past, Alice and her father reach a point of understanding. They do not magically fix everything, but they find a way to forgive each other. As the train finally arrives, you see a shift in their relationship. They decide to try and be in each other's lives again for the sake of the new baby on the way.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet stories about family secrets and healing.
